test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 18 Aug 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, and decide which of the given conclusions logically follow/s from the given statements.

**Statements:**

All toys are plastics.

All plastics are disposables.

Some toys are fibres.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some fibres are plastics.

(II) Some disposables are fibres.

(III) No fibre is a disposable.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows

solution:
**Given Statements:**

All toys are plastics.

All plastics are disposables.

Some toys are fibres.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cdab4133bad1c08b4c4d57e7ebb343854ab291a63d56c4642e22112c88071431.png] 

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some fibres are plastics → **True** (Because it is given that some toys are fibres and all toys are plastics, which means the part which is common in toys and fibres is also plastics.)

(II) Some disposables are fibres → **True** (Because it is given that some toys are fibres, all toys are plastics, and all plastics are disposables which means the part that is common in toys, fibers, and plastics is also disposables.)

(III) No fibre is a disposable → False (Because it is given that some toys are fibres, all toys are plastics, and all plastics are disposables that means there is definitely some part of fibre which is disposable)

So, only conclusion I and II follows.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.
